Asset type: a production-source transparent game sprite, single separate character. Use the attached source as the exact identity and pose reference. Preserve original geometry and paper-layer arrangement; this is a material-and-colour redraw plus specified eye removal. Clear space around the entire silhouette. Attached is Nat, my cut-paper cat mascot. Redraw him for my iOS toddler app, Lull. Keep his design exactly: the same round head, one tall pointed ear on the left, one folded-over ear on the right, tiny triangle nose, two round cheek dots, curled tail, the same proportions and the same simple shapes. Style: a real cut-paper collage photographed flat. Heavy matte construction paper with clearly visible fibres and tooth, clean scissor-cut edges, each layer casting a small soft shadow on the layer beneath, light from the upper left. Colours: body warm charcoal (#2B2523), not pure black; folded ear ochre (#D9A84E) with a slightly lighter underside; cheeks clay pink (#D99B7E); nose tan. No outlines, no gloss, no gradients, no text, no ground shadow, nothing else in the picture.

Pose: sitting and facing the viewer, exactly as in the attached picture. Important: leave the eyes out completely. The face has only the nose and the two cheek dots, and the place where the eyes were is plain charcoal paper.

Output: 1024x1024 PNG with a fully transparent background. The whole character is centred with clear space on every side and nothing cropped.
